newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Videotape fuels storm over S.Korean president's son.
newsitem.headline: Videotape fuels storm over S.Korean president's son.

text.p: A videotape showing South Korean president Kim Young-sam's son discussing a top media appointment fanned a growing political storm on Friday.
Opposition parties and the media seized on the tape as solid evidence that Kim Hyun-chul, dubbed by newspapers the "crowned prince", meddled in state affairs.

The opposition has launched an all-out attack on the president's second son since his name was linked to a bribery and influence-peddling scandal involving billions of dollars of improper loans to bankrupt Hanbo Steel Co.
Kim Hyun-chul was cleared by state prosecutors of any wrongdoing in the Hanbo affair, but the opposition has demanded a new enquiry.
In the grainy tape released on Thursday by a citizens' watch group, Kim Hyun-chul is shown and heard talking on the telephone about the appointment of the president of Yonhap Television News.
It was not clear who was on the other end of the line.
Yonhap Television is not state-owned, but its top executives are screened by the government.
The citizen's group said it obtained the video from a doctor who filmed it in his clinic in 1995.
"The prosecution must investigate Hyun-chul now there is hard evidence," the Dong-a daily said in an editorial.
"It must show that everyone is equal before the law and conduct a thorough investigation even though the president's son is involved."
The main opposition National Congress for New Politics renewed its demand for a fresh probe.
"Now that such evidence has surfaced, a probe must be reopened into Hyun-chul's meddling into government decision-making as well as into head appointments," said Park Sun-suck, a party spokeswoman.
"Hyun-chul's contacts must also be revealed."
There was no immediate reaction from Kim Hyun-chul. The presidential Blue House declined to comment.

The opposition is demanding Kim Hyun-chul appear in parliament to answer questions over his role in the Hanbo scandal. The country's number two steelmaker collapsed in January under $5.8 billion of debt.
President Kim apologised over the scandal last month. Without suggesting that his son was guilty, he banished him from public life and said he took "moral responsiblity" for Hyun-chul's behaviour.
Kim Hyun-chul played an important role in his father's election in 1992, but has no position in the administration.
The doctor who supplied the tape has been widely quoted as saying he was once was close to Kim Hyun-chul but fell out over business.
The tape has been given prominent coverage on television news broadcasts.

Kim Hyun-chul is heard mentioning a former home affairs minister for the job, which eventually went to another candidate. The minister, Kim Woo-suk, is now in custody after being arrested in the Hanbo scandal.
